messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Elevated error rate detected on prod-us-east-1 for /v1/generate (deploy ~8m ago). p95 latency x4, p99 x8, 5xx + gateway timeouts rising. Triggering pager to @sre-oncall. deploy-bot: recent deploy release/2026-03-15-ff23.

sre-oncall: ack — I'm on. Paging eng-runtime and eng-platform: @alice @bob. Pulling charts now.

alice: looking at runtime dashboards — large increase in multiplex queue depth on runtime-pool-3, KV cache miss rate spiked, long tail on token generation latencies after the deploy. stack traces show repeated cache eviction churn.

bob: can we roll the canary back? If this came with a batching heuristic change we should revert.

sre-oncall: agree. prepping rollback. anyone see an alternative quick mitigation?

alice: temporary: lower max_batch_size and reduce multiplex concurrency on the affected pods, but that's churny. rollback is cleaner.

sre-oncall: ok rolling back. Command:
```bash
./deploy rollback --env=prod --release=2026-03-14-stable --force --reason="timeout-regression-after-deploy"
```

deploy-bot: rollback accepted, initiating rollback to release/2026-03-14-stable. ETA ~3m. :gear:

support-bot: FYI support: we have 2 escalations open referencing 500s and "request timed out" from customers A and B, and an uptick in webhooks failing. Estimated impacted requests ~9-12% in the last 10m.

carol: adding provisional routing mitigation — moving /v1/generate traffic away from prod-us-east-1 to prod-us-west-2 for new sessions and shifting existing sessions to fallbacks. I'll patch global-proxy.

dave: checking model path — most errors hit redwood-13b-quant variant. Quantized execution path seems to amplify long-tail when batch heuristics change. Recommend fallback to redwood-13b-fp16 or force the non-quant path for affected pods.

alice: good catch. after rollback, we'll pin the quantized heuristic to previous config and run canary with synthetic traffic.

deploy-bot: rollback completed for prod-us-east-1 -> now at release/2026-03-14-stable.

sre-oncall: metrics update: p95 trending back down, p99 improving, 5xx rate dropped from ~4.5% to 0.8% within 2m of rollback. continuing to monitor 15m window. :white_check_mark:

erin: product note — support asked for public status update. Can someone draft a short status page message? Need estimated impact, actions taken, and next update timeline.

frank: capturing handoff notes for next oncall @grace. Root cause hypothesis: interaction between new batching/multiplex heuristic introduced in release/2026-03-15-ff23 and KV cache eviction pattern causing queue amplification on quantized model path.

frank: immediate mitigations performed: 1) rollback to previous release; 2) routing shift away from us-east-1; 3) temporary throttle on concurrency to affected runtime pool; 4) support notified and two customer tickets acknowledged.

frank: follow-ups assigned: eng-runtime (alice) to reproduce with synthetic traffic and gated canary tests; eng-ml (dave) to test quantized vs fp16 under new batching; eng-platform (bob) to add deploy gating metrics and make rollback playbook clearer.

alice: I'll run a replay suite (link: http://internal/replay/cases/timeout-regression) and attach logs.

frank: leaving detailed runbook notes in incident tracker. Handoff to @grace in 20m — please monitor alerts and confirm status page update.

sre-oncall: thanks all, marking incident as mitigated for now. Will keep channel open for postmortem steps. If we see any regression during the 15m window we'll re-escalate.

support-bot: status page draft suggestion: "We observed an increase in timeouts and server errors for the text-generation API following a recent deploy. We rolled back the release and routing changes were applied; error rates are returning to normal. We continue to monitor and will provide a full update soon."

grace: I'll take the next-watch. Thanks for the notes — will validate metric baselines and keep on top of support tickets.

incident-bot: Incident marked MITIGATED by sre-oncall. Please open a postmortem and link to this thread when ready.
_meta: Generated synthetic Slack thread for incident dataset: timeout regression after deploy, immediate rollback and handoff coordination
